items_missed: Section 2 (Probe): never asked about packing service needs, storage stops, additional stops, or whether Tommy had any worries about the move.

Section 3 (Pricing): no 'pricing is super simple' opener, no stated hourly rate per mover, no rundown of what's included (gas, truck, insurance, tools), no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch.
Section 4 (Clock): clock, minimum, and 15-min proration were all explained correctly, but there was no sense-check ('does that make sense?') after.
Section 5 (Estimate): didn't tie the parking-to-door walk distance into the time rationale, no equivalents/analogy used, traffic wasn't addressed separately from drive time.
Section 6 (Save Your Ass): skipped entirely — no mention that prep shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip.
Section 7 (Quote/Booking): never said no deposit is required, never gave office hours or how to reach the team with questions.
Section 8 (Politeness): used Tommy's name only twice (confirming the file, and the farewell) — short of the 3+ target.
Section 9 (Bonus): no rapport/humor moment beyond general politeness, and the insurance explanation covered No Worries coverage but left out the 60 cents/lb baseline liability coverage.
top_strength: Nicole handled the whole detail-confirmation efficiently in under 8 minutes and proactively surfaced both No Worries Damage Coverage and the Meet Your Mover email without being asked. She also smoothly handled a tricky ask — when Tommy wanted his old bed hauled to a dumpster, she was direct and clear: "We can only disassemble it, but we don't do disposal," and he immediately accepted that.
coaching_note: You're clean and efficient on detail confirmation, but the Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped completely — that's the highest-value section for keeping the actual time (and Tommy's bill) down, and this call was a perfect spot for it since he's already downsizing a bed. Build in the hourly rate and the 'no hidden fees' line before you give a flat dollar range, so the customer understands how you got there instead of just hearing a number. Close every call with the no-deposit line and how to reach us with questions — those are two-second additions you're leaving out.
phone_presence_notes: Consistent warm affirmations ("Awesome," "Great") and a genuine farewell, with the customer confirming he's a repeat customer and staying positive throughout, though there's no standout humor or rapport moment to push it to a 5.
